# FalconFIX — Copilot Instructions

C++20 FIX engine. CMake ≥3.16, MSVC (Windows) / GCC-Clang (Linux), GTest. Python generator in `falcongen/`.

## Layout
| Path | Purpose | Editable |
|---|---|---|
| `src/include/<module>/` | Public headers (app, config, connection, logger, runtime, session, socket, store, utils) | yes |
| `src/cpp/<module>/` | Implementation of the above | yes |
| `src/engine/{include,cpp}/FIX4.x/` | FIX protocol code (types, messages, components, session) **generated by falcongen**; built as lib `falconfix_core` | **NO** |
| `tests/<module>/` | GTest suites; `tests/support/` = helpers; `tests/main.cpp` = runner. `tests/engine/**` is generated | yes* |
| `apps/{client_fix,server_fix}/` | Example client/server executables | yes |
| `benchmark/<module>/` | Google Benchmark perf tests + `benchmark/support/` harness | yes |
| `falcongen/` | Python generator (`falcon-gen.py`, `gen_serializer_tests.py`, `code/`, `config/*.yaml`) | yes |
| `cmake/` | Macros `add_lib_custom`, `add_test_custom`, `add_app_custom`, `add_benchmark_custom`, `AddGeneratedProtocols` | rarely |
| `CMakeLists.txt`, `CMakePresets.json` | Root build config | rarely |
| `build/` | Preset build output (vcpkg deps live here) | never (generated) |

Dependency direction: `app → runtime → session → connection → socket`; session uses `engine`; never the reverse. Before touching more than one module, load skill `architecture-map`; for generated protocol code, skill `engine-layout`.

## Hard rules
- Never edit `src/engine/**` — change `falcongen/` and regenerate. `tests/engine/**` is generated too: prototype in `_tests.cpp`, then port to the generator (`falcongen/gen_serializer_tests.py`) and regenerate; see `.github/instructions/engine.instructions.md`.
- Never edit root `CMakeLists.txt` or `cmake/*.cmake` without explicit approval; new libs/tests use the existing macros.
- No `new`/`delete`, no owning raw pointers, no global mutable state.
- Session state changes go through transition methods only.
- Every change ships with GTest coverage (happy path + error + edge). No "add tests later".
- New files start with:
  ```
  // SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
  // Copyright (c) 2026 Michel Tonetti, Herik Lima, and Fabio Galuppo
  ```
  (`#` prefix in Python.)

## Build / test (incremental — reuse the same build dir)
```
# If build/windows-debug already exists, skip configure — just build incrementally.
cmake --preset windows-debug          # first time only (or linux-debug)
cmake --build --preset windows-debug  # incremental; never wipe the dir to force a rebuild
ctest --preset windows-debug --output-on-failure
```

## Style essentials (details: `.github/instructions/cpp.instructions.md`)
Namespace `falconfix` (sub: `falconfix::socket`, `falconfix::test`). Files `snake_case.h/.cpp`; classes `PascalCase`; methods/functions `camelCase`; members `m_camelCase`; constants `UPPER_CASE`. `#pragma once`. Format with `.clang-format` (Allman braces, 4 spaces, 100 cols).

## Agent behavior
- **No invention:** if a symbol, macro, preset, path, or FIX field isn't in these docs or confirmed by search/opening the file, do not guess — search or ask. A wrong symbol that fails to compile costs more than a lookup.
- **Command execution:** obey the user's most recent explicit instruction. If the user says they will run commands, do not run any — make the edits, give exact commands, wait for results. If the user authorizes execution, run them. Latest instruction overrides earlier ones; never change this policy on your own.
- **Reference examples** (copy the pattern, don't reinvent): header `src/include/connection/tcp_initiator_connection.h`; error codes/macros `src/include/utils/error_codes.h` (or skill `error-codes`); `FIXApplication` impl + message handling `tests/app/app_test.cpp`; test suite `tests/session/session_logon_tests.cpp`. (`apps/*/main.cpp` are stubs — don't copy them.)
- **Skills on demand:** `architecture-map` (cross-module), `engine-layout` (generated FIX code), `build-test`, `falcongen-regenerate`, `add-module-test`, `error-codes`.
- **Stall guard:**
- Prefer file/search tools over terminal commands; use the terminal only when no other tool can do the job, one short command at a time, and run long tasks (builds, ctest) in the background and poll.
- Do the work; don't restate these rules. Commit messages: what + why.
